JOURNALS AND NOTES IN PLAIN TEXT

Jot things down. Get beautiful pages back.

Type the way you think: a date, a few tasks, a thought, a #tag. Jot turns it into a formatted journal or notes page, ready to read, print or share. The file you wrote stays an ordinary text file: no app to keep paying for, no account, nothing that stops opening.

Why keep a journal in Jot?

01

It outlives the app.

Journals last decades; apps don't. A .jot file is plain UTF-8 text, the most durable digital format there is. If every Jot tool disappeared tomorrow, your journal would still open in Notepad.

02

It's yours, and only yours.

Nothing here has an account, a server or analytics. The workspace, the template editor and the converter run in your browser, and nothing you write is uploaded. Copy the file wherever you like.

03

Write anywhere you can type.

A phone notes app, a laptop, an e-ink typewriter like InkDeck, VS Code. The same file works in all of them, and the marks are easy to type by hand: [ ] for a task, o for an event, ### 2026-10-26 for a day.

04

Mix methods freely.

Bullet journal, morning pages, gratitude, CBT thought records, habit trackers, a weekly dashboard. 49 method guides, and none of them owns the file: use one, use five, change your mind next month.

05

Quick notes, beautiful pages.

Jot things down in a few keystrokes and get formatted pages back: dates in words, tasks ticked off, tags, margin notes, in the same handwritten style you see here, or a typed Journal or Notes style. Print them or save one page to share.

06

Numbers become charts.

Track sleep, steps, hours worked or mood as numbers, not just checkmarks. Add a chart and the week draws itself, so patterns show at a glance, while the file stays readable text.

07

Paper when you want it.

Print your journal handwritten on a dot grid, text and checkboxes aligned to the dot grid, in A5, A4, Letter or pocket size, and keep pictures and sketches beside the words in a .jotz.

NEW · THE WEEKLY DASHBOARD

Your week at a glance, in seven widgets or fewer.

Working memory holds only a handful of things at once (George Miller's "magical number seven"), so a week page works best with 5 to 7 widgets: top priorities, tasks, schedule, habits, a chart of your numbers, a scratchpad. The template editor's Weekly dashboard starter sets that up, and warns you past seven.

Write a number each day and the chart fills in, in the workspace, in the template editor's preview and in VS Code.

Make a weekly dashboardHow numbers and charts work

A week of sleep and steps, drawn from a .jot file.

NEW · HANDWRITTEN PAGES

Typed when you write it. Handwritten when you print it.

Turn on Handwritten in the workspace and your journal is written out in a pen hand, the text centred between the dot rows, and printed that way: the dots and the writing come out together on A5, A4, Letter or pocket paper.

Each letter of the pen hand comes in three shapes and every word leans a little differently, so it reads like a notebook, not a font. Boxes are drawn in pencil and ticked with a scribble. Your words stay exactly what you typed.
